event_note: No company-confirmed date or session. conviction_note: Five small, offsetting findings: a structural royalty cut and higher G&A against easier cocoa, a debt repayment and an open sale review. The sum is -0.5 and the scaled number is -0.65 (p_up 45 x abs 6.5). The lean comes from the last three prints all falling (-7.0, -5.1, -2.0) and an 18% five-day run-up on roughly $100k a day of turnover going into an unconfirmed date. The bar is unsourced, so every size is capped small. If the scored window is the sealed 10-12 bmo window, the right answer is 0 because no print lands in it.
bar: Unsourced. No consensus could be found: Earnings Whispers shows '-' for EPS and revenue (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/RMCF), and the company gives no numeric guidance (Q1 FY2027 release, https://ir.rmcf.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/317/rocky-mountain-chocolate-factory-reports-fiscal-first). findings.finding: Q1 FY2027 (quarter to 2026-05-31) showed franchise and royalty fees down 26% year on year ($1.232m vs $1.655m) because of revised franchise agreements with lower royalty and marketing fees. G&A rose 28% ($1.280m vs $1.001m) on the franchise website and delivery-platform rollout, and the net loss widened to $1.168m from $0.324m. Both are structural and carry into Q2. If royalty fees fall about 26% again against Q2 FY2026's $1.640m (about -$0.4m), total revenue lands below the year-ago $6.82m and the loss lands wider than the year-ago $0.66m, unless product sales (+3.5% in Q1 on price, plus the fifth company store from 2026-07-15) make up the difference.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 FY2027 print that first showed the royalty cut and wider loss moved -1.96% (baseline, 2026-07-14 amc). Q3 FY2026 moved -7.01% and FY2026 (2026-06-01) -5.08%. The last three prints all fell.
findings.resolves_by: 2026-10-13 if the print is 2026-10-12 amc (last year's pattern); no later than 2026-10-16 if the release comes by the 2026-10-15 10-Q deadline. This is AFTER the sealed 10-12 bmo window.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q1 numbers are public, but nobody publishes a Q2 estimate, so no bar mechanically carries the royalty cut forward. If the market had priced a wider Q2 loss, the stock would not have run up 18% in the five sessions before the print. The run-up came on the sale-leaseback, which bears on the balance sheet, not the P&L.
findings.independence: Same company document as finding 4 (cash and going concern come from the Q1 10-Q, a sibling filing). The 10-Q store table (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1616262/000119312526303159/rmcf-20260531.htm) shows total stores falling from 253 to 250 in Q1 (3 Cold Stone co-branded closures), which points the same way on royalties.

findings.finding: ICE cocoa traded about $5,600-6,650/t in August 2026, with a 28-day average of $5,928 (Farms.com, week ending 2026-08-28). RMCF's Q2 FY2026 product and retail gross profit was -$33k, which the company blamed on higher input costs and operational inefficiencies. Against that near-zero base, with cocoa well below its 2024-25 peaks and 3% price increases in place, a year-on-year gross-profit improvement in Q2 FY2027 is plausible. However, the company's own Q1 FY2027 margin fell to about 3.7% from 6.9% despite the same cost environment, so the transmission is unconfirmed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 FY2026 print that showed the gross loss moved +5.73% (baseline row 2025-10-14, which is the reaction to the 2025-10-13 amc release), so the market looked past a gross loss when revenue grew. In Q1 FY2027 the gross margin fell and the stock fell -1.96%.
findings.resolves_by: 2026-10-13 if the print is 2026-10-12 amc; no later than 2026-10-16. This is AFTER the sealed 10-12 bmo window.
findings.why_not_priced: No analyst covers the name, so nobody maps cocoa into RMCF's margin. If they had, a gross-margin recovery would already be in a bar. It is a proxy, and the company's own Q1 number contradicts it, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Proxy only. The company's Q2 FY2026 release (https://ir.rmcf.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/301/rocky-mountain-chocolate-factory-reports-second-quarter) attributes the year-ago gross loss to input costs, which sets a low base. The Q1 FY2027 release (detail/317) cuts against the finding.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-06 RMCF sold its Durango HQ, factory and warehouse for $6.6m (independent appraisal) to American Heritage Legacies, a company controlled by Interim CEO Allen Harper's family. It will use the proceeds to repay the $6.6m 12% note owed to RMC Credit Facility LLC, which is affiliated with director Steven Craig and secured on Durango, maturing 2027-09-30. RMCF leases the property back for 10 years at $624k in year one (9.45%) with 2% annual escalators. Interest falls by about $792k a year against $624k of rent, and the 2027 maturity and that lender's security go away. Expect the Q2 10-Q to carry this as a subsequent event, possibly with a gain on sale and revised going-concern or covenant language.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No earnings print has carried a financing change. The announcement itself coincides with the +18.2% five-day run-up in the baseline.
findings.resolves_by: 2026-10-13 if the print is 2026-10-12 amc; no later than 2026-10-16 (10-Q subsequent-events note). This is AFTER the sealed 10-12 bmo window.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the stock rose about 18% in five sessions after the announcement. What is not yet visible is the accounting, meaning the size of any gain, whether the TL/TNW covenant is cured and whether the going-concern paragraph is softened. These appear only in the 10-Q. What the money buys: it refinances expensive related-party debt. It does not fund growth or working capital.
findings.independence: The lender, rate and maturity come from a different document: the 2025-08-28 8-K amending the RMC note (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1616262/000143774925028281/rmcfd20250829_8k.htm), as summarised in search results. It shares the covenant question with finding 4. A separate $1.2m 12% loan from RMCF2 Credit LLC remains outstanding.

findings.finding: The Q1 FY2027 10-Q carries substantial-doubt going-concern language. It says the company breached its total-liabilities-to-tangible-net-worth covenant (5.3:1 against a 2.0:1 maximum at 2026-05-31) and that lender waivers run only through the quarter ended 2026-08-31. Cash was $609k against $4.59m of accounts payable. A $6.0m S-3 shelf became effective 2026-07-01 at a time when the stock was $0.89. The Q2 10-Q must show the covenant position at 2026-08-31 after another quarterly loss and the pre-holiday inventory build. Going-concern language is near-certain to remain, and the shelf leaves room for dilution after the print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Going-concern language and covenant breaches were in the Q1 10-Q filed with the 2026-07-14 print, which moved -1.96%. The stock fell from $2.66 (2026-05-06) to $0.89 (2026-06-30) through the 10-K, the auditor change and the CEO change.
findings.resolves_by: 2026-10-13 if the print is 2026-10-12 amc; no later than 2026-10-16. This is AFTER the sealed 10-12 bmo window.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock trades at about $1 and about 64% off its high. Nobody has said whether the waiver was extended past 2026-08-31. The 10-Q will say, and any covenant default that is not waived, or a dilutive raise, would come on top of the going-concern disclosure the market already has. Financing question answered: the money does not fund a ramp; this is covenant pressure plus a going-concern flag.
findings.independence: Shares the Q1 10-Q with finding 1. The 424B5 base prospectus (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1616262/000121390026075602/0001213900-26-075602.txt, 2026-07-06) establishes the $6.0m shelf and the $0.89 price. Finding 3's debt repayment partly offsets this one.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-11 the board disclosed under Reg FD, after the interim CEO told employees and franchisees, that it is exploring strategic alternatives including a sale, merger or going-private transaction, and that it has received third-party expressions of interest. The interim CEO controls AHR, which holds about 8.6% (810k shares), and his family has just bought the HQ. The Q1 release said a call is expected with Q2, which would be the first call since the review began, so any update or Q&A would surface there. The company says it will not comment further unless a deal is approved.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print carried a strategic-review update. Baseline reaction history has a median absolute move of 4.37%.
findings.resolves_by: 2026-10-13 if the print is 2026-10-12 amc; no later than 2026-10-16. This is AFTER the sealed 10-12 bmo window.
findings.why_not_priced: The review is public, but the stock at about $1 (market cap about $10m) carries little takeover premium. If the market expected a bid, the stock would trade at or above the $2-3 of spring 2026. The call is the first forum where management can be asked, and the sale-leaseback to an insider's family is a new data point on who may be positioning. The company's no-comment policy makes a substantive update unlikely, which is why the size is small with a wide upper tail.
findings.independence: Harper's AHR stake and appointment: 8-K item 5.02 of 2026-07-06 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1616262/000121390026075603/ea0297189-8k_rocky.htm). Related-party buyer: sale-leaseback release (detail/321), a document shared with finding 3. lessons_applied: Rule 5 (narrow proxy loses to a company number): cocoa finding cut from +0.7 to +0.3, because RMCF's own Q1 FY2027 gross margin fell despite the same cost environment.

Rule 9 ('documents beat covenant arithmetic') together with rule 4 (financing is a question): going-concern and covenant finding cut from -1.0 to -0.8. The money refinances expensive debt rather than funding a ramp, and the negative rests partly on covenant arithmetic.
Rule 6 (bar unsourced, so cap everything small): every size was already under 1.0, so no change.
